_comment: Success-score component weights, per position. Goal contributions (perf_level/perf_delta) are a weak-to-meaningless signal for defenders/goalkeepers (most keepers have 0 goals+assists both before and after a move), so their weight is shifted toward the FotMob-derived components instead - the ones actually built to differ by position (see compute_fotmob_component_pcts in build_dataset.py - FotMob's own per-match rating; goals/xG/xA/dribbles/chances-created for attacking; tackles/interceptions/clearances/recoveries for outfielders or saves/save%/goals-conceded for goalkeepers under defensive; accurate passes/90 for possession), kept separate rather than blended into one number so a player's actual profile (e.g. an attack-minded fullback vs. a purely defensive one) survives into the score. Each is only known for the subset of transfers with FotMob tenure stats for that specific bucket (data/raw/fotmob_stats_cache.csv, built by scripts/fetch_fotmob_stats.py - optional, like the resale/loan cache below) - for a row missing a bucket, that bucket's weight is dropped and the other weights renormalized, same pattern as resale_profit, independently per bucket. value_growth, value_for_money, AND rating are all deliberately FLAT across every position (0.15/0.10/0.10) - value_growth/value_for_money because they're each a single global percentile rank with no position grouping at all (unlike perf_level/defensive/etc., which are ranked within position), so there was never a real football-role reason for their weight to vary by position; rating because it's the same metric (FotMob's own overall per-match quality score) regardless of role, unlike attacking/defensive/possession which are literally different stats depending on position. value_for_money was originally flat at 0.20 (moved there from a 0.20/0.22/0.22/0.25 position-by-position spread that was really just leftover perf_level weight, not a deliberate choice) but that's still a lot of weight on one fee-vs-performance metric, so it's now 0.10 - the freed 0.10 is routed into attacking/defensive/possession (scaled proportionally per position, same mechanism as the original flattening), NOT into rating, which is funded separately (see below). rating's move up to a flat 0.10 is funded entirely from perf_level/perf_delta/playing_time (scaled down proportionally, preserving their relative ratio to each other) rather than from value_growth/value_for_money (kept flat in their own right) or attacking/defensive/possession (reserved for role-specific tuning - see _sub_positions_comment). resale_profit's weight is NOT the flat number below - it varies by tenure length per resale_weight_curve (a quick flip weights resale heavily since that's often the point of the deal; a long career barely moves regardless of the eventual sale price, since the club already extracted years of value). The number here is just the weight at the curve's ~2-year reference point, kept for documentation. Only known for the ~17% of transfers where the club actually resold the player for a recorded fee - for the rest it's excluded and the other weights are renormalized to sum to 1 (see build_dataset.py). Shared by scripts/build_dataset.py (computes the label) and app/main.py (labels the 'why this score' explanation). Each position row (including resale_profit) must sum to 1.0.
_sub_positions_comment: Sub-position weight overrides (see build_dataset.py's lookup_weights and SUB_POSITION_WEIGHTS) - a player's actual career-wide fielded sub-position (from game_lineups.csv, not the single undated label in players.csv - see load_actual_sub_positions) selects one of these rows INSTEAD of the broad position row above, when one exists for it; percentile ranking itself still groups by the broad position above, only the weights differ - a Centre-Back is still ranked against all Defenders, just weighted differently once ranked. Only sub-positions with a real, well-established difference in role expectations get an explicit row here (Defensive Midfield vs. Attacking Midfield vs. wide midfield; Centre-Back vs. full-back; winger); Central Midfield, Centre-Forward, Second Striker, and Goalkeeper fall back to their broad position's row unchanged - either because that IS the broad default's implicit profile (Central Midfield, Centre-Forward), the position has no sub-split at all (Goalkeeper), or the sample is too thin in this dataset for a confident, distinct opinion (Second Striker, ~300 players total before any transfer/appearance filters). Each row still needs perf_level/perf_delta/value_growth/playing_time/value_for_money/rating/attacking/defensive/possession/resale_profit and must sum to 1.0, same as the broad rows. The directional idea throughout: dial perf_level+perf_delta+attacking (the same 'attacking output' bloc fold_perf_level_into_attacking folds into one number) down for a defense-oriented sub-position and up for an attack-oriented one, moving that weight into defensive/possession instead - the FotMob buckets that actually differ by role. Attacking Midfield's possession in particular is set explicitly (0.13, alongside Winger/Defensive Midfield) rather than purely mechanically - a naive proportional scaling during an earlier weight change had compressed it to 0.03, far below every comparable sub-position, which made no football sense for a possession-heavy #10 role. Full-back's defensive is likewise set explicitly to 0.26 (funded from perf_level/perf_delta/attacking) rather than left at the smaller mechanically-derived value - a full-back is still fundamentally a defender, and their weight profile now sits close to Centre-Back's (defensive 0.26 vs. 0.29, attacking 0.03 vs. 0.01), just with a little more license to contribute going forward. value_growth, value_for_money, and rating are flat 0.15/0.10/0.10 here too, same as the broad rows above and for the same reason - none of the three have a football-role basis to vary at this level either. Caicedo (Chelsea, Defensive Midfield) is the motivating case - see the README section on sub-position weighting.

resale_weight_curve._comment: resale_weight(tenure_years) = min + (max - min) * exp(-tenure_years / decay_years). A few months' tenure -> ~18-20% weight; ~2 years -> ~8.6% (close to the old flat 8%); 6+ years -> under 3%.
